person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the term biostimulant itself - its competing definitions, synonyms and regulatory categories
span.quote: The task of defining the biological basis of biostimulants as a class of compounds, however, is made more complex by the diverse sources of biostimulants present in the market, which include bacteria, fungi, seaweeds, higher plants, animals and humate-containing raw materials, and the wide diversity of industrial processes utilized in their preparation.

span.label: what a biostimulant is, such that the category can be distinguished from fertilisers, hormones and pesticides
span.quote: To distinguish biostimulants from the existing legislative product categories including essential nutrients, pesticides, or plant hormones a biostimulant should not solely function by virtue of the presence of elements or compounds of known function. We propose, therefore, a definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.”

span.label: a proposed definition turning on emergent properties, and a table of the competing definitions it replaces
span.quote: To distinguish biostimulants from the existing legislative product categories including essential nutrients, pesticides, or plant hormones a biostimulant should not solely function by virtue of the presence of elements or compounds of known function. We propose, therefore, a definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.”

span.label: critique
span.quote: The elucidation of the biological basis of biostimulant function is a prerequisite for the development of science-based biostimulant industry and sound regulations governing these compounds.

span.label: plant productivity improved by products whose active principle is not a known nutrient, hormone or pesticide

span.label: a systematic review of the field's definitions, terms and synonyms, including verbatim translation of the Russian literature
span.term: a systematic review of the field's definitions, terms and synonyms, including verbatim translation of the Russian literature
span.quote: The task of defining the biological basis of biostimulants as a class of compounds, however, is made more complex by the diverse sources of biostimulants present in the market, which include bacteria, fungi, seaweeds, higher plants, animals and humate-containing raw materials, and the wide diversity of industrial processes utilized in their preparation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A DEFINITION BUILT ON IRREDUCIBILITY: the effect must come from emergent properties of the whole complex and NOT be the sole consequence of any known constituent - so a product whose activity is explained by its nutrients is, by this definition, not a biostimulant
span.quote: To distinguish biostimulants from the existing legislative product categories including essential nutrients, pesticides, or plant hormones a biostimulant should not solely function by virtue of the presence of elements or compounds of known function. We propose, therefore, a definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.”

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WHY THE DEFINITION IS SHAPED THAT WAY: it exists to allow that biological function can be modulated by mixtures for which no explicit mode of action has been established
span.quote: The definition provided here is important as it emphasizes the principle that biological function can be positively modulated through application of molecules, or mixtures of molecules, for which an explicit mode of action has not been defined.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: VALIDATION MOVED FROM MODE TO MECHANISM: efficacy, safety and a broad mechanism are asked for, and the specific mode is not - a regulatory position derived from the definition rather than from an experiment
span.quote: Given the difficulty in determining a “mode of action” for a biostimulant, and recognizing the need for the market in biostimulants to attain legitimacy, we suggest that the focus of biostimulant research and validation should be upon proof of efficacy and safety and the determination of a broad mechanism of action, without a requirement for the determination of a specific mode of action.

span.label: THREE NAMED AUTHORITIES DISAGREEING ABOUT WHAT KIND OF THING A DEFINITION SHOULD BE, IN ONE PARAGRAPH: `Basak (2008) proposed that biostimulants could be classified depending on the MODE OF ACTION AND THE ORIGIN of the active ingredient`; `Bulgari et al. (2015) proposed that biostimulants should be classified ON THE BASIS OF THEIR ACTION IN THE PLANTS or, on the PHYSIOLOGICAL PLANT RESPONSES RATHER THAN ON THEIR COMPOSITION`; `Du Jardin (2015) ... any definition should focus on the AGRICULTURAL FUNCTIONS, NOT ON THE NATURE OF THEIR CONSTITUENTS NOR ON THEIR MODES OF ACTIONS.` Composition, physiological response, agricultural function - and Du Jardin's rule explicitly rejects Basak's criterion.
span.quote: Several concepts have been proposed to define plant biostimulants. Basak (2008), proposed that biostimulants could be classified depending on the mode of action and the origin of the active ingredient while Bulgari et al. (2015), proposed that “biostimulants should be classified on the basis of their action in the plants or, on the physiological plant responses rather than on their composition.” Du Jardin (2015), however, has emphasized the importance of the final impact on plant productivity when he suggests that “any definition of biostimulants should focus on the agricultural functions of biostimulants, not on the nature of their constituents nor on their modes of actions.”

span.label: AND THE PAPER REDUCES THE DISPUTE TO A BINARY: `biostimulants could be defined by their DEMONSTRATED MODE OF ACTION AND ORIGIN, OR SOLELY BY THEIR DEMONSTRATED BENEFICIAL IMPACT ON PLANT PRODUCTIVITY.` Define by how it works, or define by what it achieves.
span.quote: Thus, biostimulants could be defined by their demonstrated mode of action and origin, or solely by their demonstrated beneficial impact on plant productivity

span.label: A DEFINITION WRITTEN TO POLICE A MARKET: `Given the state of PUBLIC MISTRUST of many biostimulant products, it is necessary to provide a definition that EXPLICITLY DENIES THE USE OF THIS TERM for products that do not have biological efficacy OR HAVE EFFICACY ONLY BY VIRTUE OF THE INCLUSION OF KNOWN PLANT HORMONES OR NUTRIENTS.` The definition's stated job is to exclude bad actors, not to describe a natural kind.
span.quote: Given the state of public mistrust of many “biostimulant” products, it is necessary to provide a definition of biostimulants that explicitly denies the use of this term for products that do not have biological efficacy or have efficacy only by virtue of the inclusion of known plant hormones or nutrients

span.label: ONE THING, THREE PLACEMENTS, THREE PAPERS: `are biostimulants PGRs? Historically, biostimulants have been considered AS A SUBGROUP OF GROWTH REGULATORS (Herve, 1994), AS PLANT GROWTH REGULATORS (Huang, 2007), and AS SUBGROUP OF BIOREGULATORS (Basak, 2008).` Subgroup of one thing, identical to it, subgroup of a third - 1994, 2007, 2008.
span.quote: One area of significant challenge is evoked in the question “are biostimulants PGRs?” Historically, biostimulants have been considered as a subgroup of growth regulators (Herve, 1994), as plant growth regulators (Huang, 2007), and as subgroup of bioregulators (Basak, 2008)

span.label: TEN NAMES IN ONE SENTENCE, AND THE TERM DECLARED POORLY DEFINED: it is `POORLY DEFINED and includes many products that have VARIOUSLY BEEN DESCRIBED AS BIOGENIC STIMULANTS, METABOLIC ENHANCERS, PLANT STRENGTHENERS, POSITIVE PLANT GROWTH REGULATORS, ELICITORS, ALLELOPATHIC PREPARATION, PLANT CONDITIONERS, PHYTOSTIMULATORS, BIOFERTILISERS, or biofertiliser/biostimulant`. Table 1 then gives each its original definition and reference, with the Russian sources translated verbatim.
span.quote: Currently, poorly defined and includes many products that have variously been described as biogenic stimulants, metabolic enhancers, plant strengtheners, positive plant growth regulators, elicitors, allelopathic preparation, plant conditioners, phytostimulators, biofertilisers, or biofertiliser/biostimulant (Table 1)

span.label: AND THE PAPER MAKES THE CLAIM THIS PROJECT EXISTS TO TEST, IN ITS CONCLUSION: the category will `SERVE AS A CRITICAL DRIVER OF DISCOVERY ... and will inevitably lead to the identification of novel biological phenomenon, pathways and processes THAT WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN DISCOVERED IF THE CATEGORY OF BIOSTIMULANTS DID NOT EXIST, OR WAS NOT CONSIDERED LEGITIMATE.` A category credited with enabling the discoveries made under it - naming as a research instrument rather than a label.
span.quote: serve as a critical driver of discovery in this realm and will inevitably lead to the identification of novel biological phenomenon, pathways and processes that would not have been discovered if the category of biostimulants did not exist, or was not considered legitimate

span.label: The definitional problem is attributed to the SUBJECT MATTER, not to carelessness: the sources run from bacteria and fungi to seaweeds, higher plants, animals and humates, with a matching diversity of industrial processes
span.quote: The task of defining the biological basis of biostimulants as a class of compounds, however, is made more complex by the diverse sources of biostimulants present in the market, which include bacteria, fungi, seaweeds, higher plants, animals and humate-containing raw materials, and the wide diversity of industrial processes utilized in their preparation.

span.label: The paper states that the biological basis must be elucidated BEFORE a science-based industry and sound regulation are possible - so its own definition is offered ahead of the evidence it says is needed
span.quote: The elucidation of the biological basis of biostimulant function is a prerequisite for the development of science-based biostimulant industry and sound regulations governing these compounds.

span.label: One of the definitions the review collects calls the term itself AMBIGUOUS, which is a limitation of the field the paper is summarising rather than of the paper
span.quote: “An ambiguous term used to encompass non-nutritional growth-promoting substances such as microbes, plant growth hormones, soil conditioners and microbe energy sources.”

span.label: the definitions collected here disagree about whether hormones may be present at all: one regulatory definition PROHIBITS phytohormones while another says the important benefits rest on hormonal activity
span.quote: It must be remind that the biostimulant activity does not have to derive from the addition of phytohormones (Attached 6, codicil 4.1).

span.label: the Russian-language definitions are given in verbatim word-for-word translation, so the terminological differences survive rather than being smoothed into English usage
span.quote: Translation from Russian publications into English is verbatim (word for word, literatim) References “Every living tissue (human, animal and plants), when exposed to unfavorable, but non-lethal conditions, undergoes biochemical restructuring with the formation in it of special substances which are biogenic stimulators of non-specific nature, stimulating the life reactions of the organism, in which they introduced in, one way or another.

span.label: Biostimulators
span.quote: “An ambiguous term used to encompass non-nutritional growth-promoting substances such as microbes, plant growth hormones, soil conditioners and microbe energy sources.”

span.label: phyllosphere
span.quote: “Products intended to protect plants against harmful organisms by stimulating defence mechanisms in the plant or by competing with harmful organisms for space and nutrients in the phyllosphere or rhizosphere.”

span.label: rhizosphere
span.quote: “Products intended to protect plants against harmful organisms by stimulating defence mechanisms in the plant or by competing with harmful organisms for space and nutrients in the phyllosphere or rhizosphere.”

span.label: plant growth regulators
span.quote: “From a legal point of view, biostimulants can contain traces of natural plant hormones, but their biological action should not be ascribed to them, otherwise they should be registered as plant growth regulators” (Bulgari et al., 2015)

span.quote: Several concepts have been proposed to define plant biostimulants. Basak (2008), proposed that biostimulants could be classified depending on the mode of action and the origin of the active ingredient while Bulgari et al. span.label: biostimulant - THIS PAPER'S PROPOSED SENSE (2017): defined by EMERGENT PROPERTIES OF THE COMPLEX, and explicitly NOT by the presence of known nutrients, growth regulators or protective compounds. The differentia is what the effect is NOT reducible to
span.quote: To distinguish biostimulants from the existing legislative product categories including essential nutrients, pesticides, or plant hormones a biostimulant should not solely function by virtue of the presence of elements or compounds of known function. We propose, therefore, a definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.”

span.label: biostimulant - the 1991 sense, Russo and Berlyn: “materials of little or no fertilizer value that accelerate plant growth” - defined by what it is worth as a fertiliser
span.quote: “Materials of little or no fertilizer value that accelerate plant growth, usually when used at low concentrations.”

span.label: biostimulant - the 1992 sense, Schmidt: PLANT HORMONE-CONTAINING substances - which the 2017 definition explicitly rules out
span.quote: “Plant hormone-containing substances that can stimulate growth when exogenously applied.”

span.label: biostimulant - the 2001 sense, McCarty: a term the literature itself calls AMBIGUOUS, covering microbes, hormones, soil conditioners and microbe energy sources
span.quote: “An ambiguous term used to encompass non-nutritional growth-promoting substances such as microbes, plant growth hormones, soil conditioners and microbe energy sources.”

span.label: biostimulant - the 2003 sense, Beard in Schmidt et al.: defined by a RESIDUAL - a response that cannot be attributed to traditional plant nutrients
span.quote: An organic material that, when applied in small quantities, enhances plant growth and development such that the response cannot be attributed to application of traditional plant nutrients.

span.label: biostimulant - the 2001 sense quoted by Sharma: a PLANT-PROTECTION product working by stimulating defence or by competing with harmful organisms - a definition the others do not share at all
span.quote: “Products intended to protect plants against harmful organisms by stimulating defence mechanisms in the plant or by competing with harmful organisms for space and nutrients in the phyllosphere or rhizosphere.”

span.label: mode of action - the SPECIFIC pathway, which the paper says is hard to establish for a biostimulant and should NOT be required for validation
span.quote: Given the difficulty in determining a “mode of action” for a biostimulant, and recognizing the need for the market in biostimulants to attain legitimacy, we suggest that the focus of biostimulant research and validation should be upon proof of efficacy and safety and the determination of a broad mechanism of action, without a requirement for the determination of a specific mode of action.

span.label: mechanism of action - the BROAD account, which the paper says validation should require instead. TWO NEAR-SYNONYMS SEPARATED, WITH A REGULATORY CONSEQUENCE ATTACHED TO THE SPLIT
span.quote: Given the difficulty in determining a “mode of action” for a biostimulant, and recognizing the need for the market in biostimulants to attain legitimacy, we suggest that the focus of biostimulant research and validation should be upon proof of efficacy and safety and the determination of a broad mechanism of action, without a requirement for the determination of a specific mode of action.

span.label: biostimulant - THE NUTRITIONAL SENSE: it contributes to crop nutrition and healthy development by its mode of action
span.quote: Natural or synthetic products of either mineral or organic composition that by their mode of action positively contribute to crop nutrition and the development of healthy plants.

span.label: biostimulant - THE EXPLICITLY NON-NUTRITIONAL SENSE: the aim is NOT to supply nutrition but to stimulate metabolism
span.quote: Are organic products composed of peptides, amino acids, polysaccharides, peptides, humic acids, and/or phytohormones, etc. for immediate uptake and availability within the plant.

span.label: biostimulant - THE HORMONE-EXCLUDING SENSE, where phytohormones are PROHIBITED by regulation
span.quote: It must be remind that the biostimulant activity does not have to derive from the addition of phytohormones (Attached 6, codicil 4.1).

span.label: biostimulant - THE HORMONE-DEPENDENT SENSE, where the important benefits are said to REST on influencing hormonal activity
span.quote: Many important benefits of biostimulants are based on their ability to influence hormonal activity.

span.label: biostimulant - THE NEGATIVE/REGULATORY SENSE, defined by what it is not: neither a fertilizer nor a pesticide
span.quote: Materials that are neither a fertilizer nor a pesticide, but when applied to a plant will enhance their health, growth, and protection.

span.label: biostimulant - THE MICROORGANISM SENSE, where the biostimulant is a living organism rather than a substance
span.quote: Both biocontrol microorganisms (BCMs) and plant growth-promoting microorganisms (PGPMs) can be defined as “biostimulant microorganisms,” able to foster plant growth and defence against pathogens throughout the crop life cycle, from seed germination to plant maturity.

span.label: biostimulant - THE STRESS-MITIGATION SENSE, acting through the plant's own innate defence responses
span.quote: Single compounds or mixtures of compounds which mitigate the effects caused by abiotic stress agents, through the induction of innate plant defense responses.

span.label: biostimulant - THE EFFICIENCY SENSE, defined by enhancing nutrient use efficiency alongside an existing fertilisation plan
span.quote: Material that, when applied to a plant, seed, soil or growing media - in conjunction with established fertilization plans, enhances the plant’s nutrient use efficiency, or provides other direct or indirect benefits to plant development or stress response.

span.label: `biostimulant` - DEFINED BY EXCLUSION FROM TWO LEGAL CATEGORIES: `biostimulants CANNOT BY DEFINITION BE PESTICIDES OR FERTILIZERS`, with seven citations behind the exclusion. The category's edges are drawn by its neighbours.
span.quote: Likewise, biostimulants cannot by definition be pesticides or fertilizers (Russo and Berlyn, 1991; Karnok, 2000; Hamza and Suggars, 2001; Banks and Percival, 2012; Du Jardin, 2012; Torre et al., 2013, 2016)

span.label: `biostimulant` - AND THE BOUNDARY WITH PGRs IS AN ATTRIBUTION RULE, NOT A COMPOSITION RULE: `biostimulants CAN CONTAIN traces of natural plant hormones, BUT THEIR BIOLOGICAL ACTION SHOULD NOT BE ASCRIBED TO THEM, OTHERWISE THEY SHOULD BE REGISTERED AS PLANT GROWTH REGULATORS.` The same bottle is one product or the other depending on what its effect is credited to.
span.quote: “From a legal point of view, biostimulants can contain traces of natural plant hormones, but their biological action should not be ascribed to them, otherwise they should be registered as plant growth regulators” (Bulgari et al., 2015)

span.quote: Given the difficulty in determining a “mode of action” for a biostimulant, and recognizing the need for the market in biostimulants to attain legitimacy, we suggest that the focus of biostimulant research and validation should be upon proof of efficacy and safety and the determination of a broad mechanism of action, without a requirement for the determination of a specific mode of action.

We propose, therefore, a definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.”

span.label: biostimulant —distinct-from→ essential plant nutrients
span.quote: To distinguish biostimulants from the existing legislative product categories including essential nutrients, pesticides, or plant hormones a biostimulant should not solely function by virtue of the presence of elements or compounds of known function. We propose, therefore, a definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.”

span.label: biostimulant —distinct-from→ plant protective compounds
span.quote: To distinguish biostimulants from the existing legislative product categories including essential nutrients, pesticides, or plant hormones a biostimulant should not solely function by virtue of the presence of elements or compounds of known function. We propose, therefore, a definition of a biostimulant as “a formulated product of biological origin that improves plant productivity as a consequence of the novel or emergent properties of the complex of constituents and not as a sole consequence of the presence of known essential plant nutrients, plant growth regulators, or plant protective compounds.”

span.label: biostimulators are explicitly said NOT to substitute for fertilisers or mineral nutrient sources, in a definition that otherwise credits them with improving growth
span.quote: Agents which at very low concentrations improve the basic biochemical processes in plants and soil, and thereby improve the growth and development of plants, and increase their resistance to stress.

span.label: one definition insists the activity is neither nutritional nor a direct action on the stressor - the compound works only by raising the plant's own capability
span.quote: Compounds of biological origin and should act by increasing natural capabilities of plants to cope with stresses.

span.label: the industry council definition: stimulating natural processes for nutrient uptake, efficiency and abiotic stress tolerance, with no direct action against pests
span.quote: Contain substance(s) and/or micro-organisms whose function when applied to plants or the rhizosphere is to stimulate natural processes to enhance/benefit nutrient uptake, nutrient efficiency, tolerance to abiotic stress, and crop quality.

span.label: the definition by exclusion: substances and materials other than nutrients and pesticides that modify plant physiology
span.quote: Substances and materials, with the exception of nutrients and pesticides, which, when applied to plants, seeds or growing substrates in specific formulations, have the capacity to modify physiological processes of plants in a way that provides potential benefits to growth, development and/or stress response.

span.label: the small-quantity criterion: an organic material whose response cannot be attributed to traditional plant nutrients
span.quote: Is an organic material that, when applied in small quantities, enhances plant growth and development such that the response cannot be attributed to the application of traditional plant nutrients.

span.label: the safety criterion written into one national definition - no risk to human, animal or natural environment
span.quote: They mean inorganic and organic substances or its mixtures positively affecting plant development or other physiological processes in plants.

span.label: a patent-style definition listing bio-stimulatory activity as everything from sugar generation to allelopathy
span.quote: The term “bio-stimulatory” means according to the invention, if not otherwise specified, an activity or efficacy which stimulates, increases or improves many different processes in the plant or plant parts, such as improved generation of growth promoting substances like sugars and amino acids, improved adequate supply of cells with available nutrients and growth regulators, enhanced cell metabolism, improved cell decontamination, enhanced immune defense, promotion of growth and yield, induction of systemic acquired resistance (SAR), inhibition of growth and yield of competing plants (allelopathy).

span.label: the phytostimulator definition, which locates the activity in a microorganism that changes growth-regulator concentrations
span.quote: Microorganism with the ability to produce or change the concentration of growth regulators such as indole acetic acid, gibberellic acid, cytokinins and ethylene.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2016.02049.
